note: Census of the product families (plan file 29 §4.4, package C0c): the event types the reducer switches on, read from its source at run time, and the waivers, each with its reason. Exports are read from the modules when the recorder loads them; nothing here lists them, so deleting an export needs no edit here unless a waiver names it (a waiver of something that no longer exists fails the census).

unrecordable.test: performs one revert lookup for session-less streaming parts
unrecordable.reason: the test counts reads of a revert_transaction accessor and expects exactly one: a performance assertion, not behaviour; the recorder never calls a getter, so the case cannot carry the value (design §2.7)

tests: passes statuses through when no guard is registered
coerces retry to idle while guard is active
does not affect other sessions
passes busy through unchanged while guard is active
schedules a re-abort when retry arrives while guard is active
debounces re-aborts and caps total attempts
idle clears the guard so later retry statuses are authoritative
clearAbortGuard restores authoritative statuses (new local send)
guard expires after TTL so live state wins again
keeps a stopped long-backoff retry guarded through its advertised deadline
does not slide a relative retry deadline when the same status is repeated
skips deferred re-abort when guard cleared before the timer fires
re-registering after a re-abort resets the budget
unrecordable.reason: the abort guard's own tests call clearAbortGuard and filterSessionStatusThroughAbortGuard themselves, which are ports of the reducer; the reducer hands out no closure (its results are data), so no reducer code can hide behind these calls, and the reducer has no step here

unrecordable.test: clears only resend markers owned by released sessions
unrecordable.reason: the test calls isCommittedRevertResendInFlight itself, a port of the reducer; the reducer hands out no closure (its results are data), so no reducer code can hide behind the call

unrecordable.test: the abort guard never re-aborts a session that is waiting on a question
unrecordable.reason: the test calls filterSessionStatusThroughAbortGuard itself, a port of the reducer; the reducer hands out no closure (its results are data), so no reducer code can hide behind the call

tests: session.idle clears the guard before it writes the idle status
session.idle clears the guard even when the status is already idle and nothing is written
session.error clears the guard before it writes the idle status
a user message that advances the turn writes user activity before it clears the guard, and the message list after
a replayed older user message writes the list and leaves the guard active
unrecordable.reason: the test wraps the draft in a Proxy of its own to observe the order in which the reducer writes; the recorder never runs a foreign Proxy's traps, so the case cannot carry the value (design §2.7)

tests: a begun resend is in flight until it ends, for that session and message only
beginning the same resend twice needs only one end
ending a resend that was never begun, or another message's, changes nothing
never reports a resend with an empty session id or a missing or empty message id as in flight, and an end with such ids leaves a real resend in flight
clearing a session removes all of its resends and none of a session whose id it prefixes
clearing takes any iterable, skips empty ids, and clears several sessions at once
a message id holding the key separator collides with a session id holding it, so both read as in flight
clearing a session whose id holds the key separator also clears another session's resend that shares the prefix
clearing a session leaves another session's resend in flight and does not stop the cleared session from beginning a new one
unrecordable.reason: the test calls the committed-revert resend functions itself (begin, end, lookup, clear), which are ports of the reducer; the reducer hands out no closure (its results are data), so no reducer code can hide behind the call

excludedFiles.reason: the mock-module layer is harmless on it since package C0c2 (17/17 and 114 assertions with the layer alone, as plain), but it cannot be recorded cleanly, for two reasons of the test itself (C0c2 report, shown by recording it alone twice with product.mjs --runs=2, twice): every one of its 11 cases is unrecordable as global-defined:document and global-defined:window (its DOM helper defines both as data properties the recorder did not wrap); and every one of its 11 cases hands the engine a directory named after the process id (devryan-model-controls-hydration-<pid>: in 10 cases as the input's directory, in one inside a message's path), so their inputs differ between recordings. Its only family use is optimistic's applyOptimisticAdd and applyOptimisticRemove, which sync tests also exercise

noFrame.reason: sync-context.tsx hands the entry itself to a promise, scopedClient.session.messages(...).then(unwrapMessageRecordsResult), where it materializes a session and where it reconnects, so the job that calls it has no frame; a test that does the same is not told apart (docs/TESTING.md)
